rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 23 'The reasons for personal-first land in Phase 3' — a forward pointer, but it names the destination heading explicitly (Phase 3, an actual `##` that exists at chunk 5) instead of leaning on an unresolved pronoun; §12's own 'name the thing' fix is exactly this shape, so it stays inside. All in-file backward references resolve against an earlier chunk of the same file: chunk 5 line 58 'wrote it in Phase 1' → chunk 1; 'Phase 2's invoke-and-critique' → chunk 3; chunk 4 line 52 'Module 3 installs' and chunk 7 line 71 'Module 4 reads this skill' are arc-earned module-name vocabulary (carve-out). Chunk 7 line 74 'came over at the fork' resolves via the session-artifacts carve-out — same paragraph already names 'the side-quest worktree' as the live session state in front of the student.

No 'the opening lecture said' style backward callback into another file's content anywhere in the body. Closest candidate: chunk 7 line 71 'Module 4 reads this skill' — names the destination module by number, doesn't quote or locate content inside it by position, and functions as a closer pointing forward (permitted per §2's own text on closers).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw' callback to another exercise or lecture's beat anywhere in body. The only backward references (chunk 5 line 58 'Phase 1', 'Phase 2's invoke-and-critique') point at this same file's own earlier `##` chunks (governed by rule 1, verified above), not at a sibling module beat — rule 3's failure shape (a dead cross-beat reference) doesn't apply here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File contains no guess-before-reveal / predict-then-watch instruction anywhere in the body; the exercise's shape is author-then-invoke-then-critique, not a demo-and-guess beat.

Closest candidate: chunk 2 (lines 29-33, shortest non-title chunk) — but it carries two self-contained instructive bullets (a concrete good-answer example plus a push-back move), not a bare wait-state. Every one of the 7 body chunks carries a standalone instructive or evaluative claim.

Checked all 7 non-title headers against their own chunk content. Closest edge case: chunk 5 header 'Phase 3: Ship the skill personal-first' (line 54) vs. content 'The skill is already shipped... There is no separate install step' (line 58) — header names the act, content confirms it already landed; that's the header being true of its chunk, not contradicted by it. No header/content mismatch found.

Checked all 5 sub-items across all 8 chunks. `grep -n 'Not [A-Z][a-z]*\. Not'` on the file → 0 hits, no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction. No anaphora/epistrophe triples found. No self-grading superlative found (closest: chunk 0 line 11 'test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram' — a claim about a failure mode in general, not praise of this exercise's own value; chunk 0 line 13 'the longest beat in Module 3' grades duration/pacing, not usefulness). No number-with-retraction pattern (file carries no hedged numbers, only plain durations like 'Time: 20 minutes'). No verb-triplet with an empty leg. Chunk 4 line 49 'same-window self-charity' is a coined handle naming a real mechanism (invoke-then-self-grade in one context window), not an abstraction-noun stack standing in for something concrete.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 line 13: '> **Quick timebox note.** This is the longest beat in Module 3 and the place where authoring conversations spiral.' — 'beat' is one of rule 8's own named specimens of maintainer/authorial dialect (curriculum-designer shorthand for a bounded activity segment), used here in exactly that sense, on the title-slide callout every student and trainer reads first. No carve-out covers it: it isn't the ordinary-engineering-verb sense of 'surface', not a canonical `##`-section name, not a locked file's attested scheme, and not a rule quoted as a specimen — it's plain narration using repo-internal shorthand. Harm: an engineer in the room either doesn't parse 'beat' (drumbeat? heartbeat? story beat?) or reads it as design-jargon rather than plain pacing talk, which is exactly the register break §8 exists to prevent on a projected slide. Confirmed unexempted: line 13 sits above the `<!-- maintainer -->` cut (line 76) with no fenced block anywhere in the raw file, and the maintainer block carries no dated accept-note authorizing this word. Fix is trivial and doesn't touch the claim: swap 'beat' for a plain pacing word.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap 'beat' for a plain word an engineer would use for a time-boxed stretch — e.g. 'stretch', 'segment', or 'activity' ('This is the longest stretch in Module 3...').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n '\*\*' curriculum/exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md` on lines 1-75 (body) → hits only at 3,5,7,9,11,13,67,74, all widget/label chrome (Time:/Window:/What you do:/What you build:/The point:/Quick timebox note./What happened:/Note), matching the file's own dated accept-note ('Emphasis pass 2026-07-09, Antti-directed') listing exactly that chrome set as untouched. Zero bold spans inside narrative bullet prose in any chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -rn 'author-test-strategy-skill' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/earn-the-trust.md` → line 41: '[Exercise: Author your test-strategy skill](exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md)', a standard module-3 exercise include. File carries no `<!--flag:module:X-->`/`<!--flag:no-module:X-->` runtime forks, so none of its 8 chunks can be resolved-away by `applyContentFlags`; it composes as a plain `.phase--exercise` include like every other exercise file, one of the two selectors `buildDeckModel` walks. No signal any section is deck-dropped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 6 of 7 body `##` headers are imperative or Phase-labels ('Answer from how your codebase really tests', 'Sharpen the skill from what came back', 'Decide if it graduates to the team', 'Phase 1/2/3: ...'). Closest edge case: chunk 7 'What this sets up' (line 69) — not imperative, not a declarative law-claim, but it matches §15's own explicit non-violation category, 'orientation headers' (cf. its examples 'You are here', 'The far half opens'): it orients the reader to forward-looking context rather than posing as a declaration. (A prior instance of this file's slides verdict flagged this same heading as a rule-15 open question before the compendium carried this carve-out; the carve-out now resolves it — the rule moved, not the body.)
